research_finding.hypothesis: If admitted_prototype_traces is not itself guaranteed content-addressed before this boundary, a registry entry could be stored beneath a claimed prototype_trace_sha256 key whose JCS bytes do not hash to that key. Semantic cross-bindings may still match downstream training/transition fields, so dataset admission would be relying on external registry key integrity rather than proving the prototype evidence identity it names.
research_finding.counterhypothesis: admitted_prototype_traces may be defined as a previously verified content-addressed registry whose key/content identity is guaranteed by its producer, making local rehash at DatasetAdmission intentionally redundant.
research_finding.why_material: The current producer explicitly defines prototype evidence identity by JCS content hash, and outcome receipts already receive an analogous canonical key/content identity verification inside the dataset gate. A prototype registry that is merely keyed by an asserted hash would weaken provenance symmetry at the training-admission boundary.
